name: needle-in-haystack
description: A single distinctive needle buried in repetitive distractor lines, used to measure whether a compaction technique keeps the needle recoverable instead of dropping it with the noise.
disclaimer: Cases are synthetic and self-authored — not sampled from, or submitted to, any external benchmark. The public benchmarks below are referenced only as task-category analogs so readers can anchor the needle-in-a-haystack retrieval task; these numbers are not scores on those benchmarks.

related_benchmarks.name: Needle In A Haystack
related_benchmarks.note: The original pressure test: hide one fact in a long context and ask for it back — the exact shape of these cases.

related_benchmarks.name: RULER (NIAH tasks)
related_benchmarks.note: Parameterized single/multi-needle retrieval over synthetic haystacks, which our filler-plus-needle construction mirrors.

related_benchmarks.name: Lost in the Middle
related_benchmarks.note: Shows retrieval accuracy depends on where the needle sits; motivates keeping every needle recoverable regardless of position.
